# Intervention Identification and Selection

## Food Environment Constraints

Through food environment mapping, we identified systemic constraints 
affecting LMI consumers in Hanoi spanning affordability, convenience, 
traceability, and trust. Existing coping strategies — informal sourcing, 
online purchasing, self-production, social networks — remain insufficient 
to ensure consistent access to safe vegetables.

## Workshop Process

Four focus groups drawn from the same participant pool discussed two 
guiding questions:

1. Which aspects of the food environment need improvement to better 
support safe vegetable consumption among LMI households in inner-city Hanoi?
2. What feasible and context-appropriate interventions can address 
the identified challenges?

Candidate interventions were evaluated against three criteria: 
(1) feasibility, (2) expected effectiveness, and (3) availability 
of actors capable of implementation.

## Intervention Longlist and Selection

```{r intervention-table, echo=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

interventions <- data.frame(
  No = 1:10,
  Intervention = c(
    "Establishing social media groups (Facebook/Zalo) for discounted purchasing",
    "Adapting PGS-based internal monitoring to reduce VietGAP certification costs",
    "Technical measures and state incentive programs to reduce production and retail costs",
    "Communication interventions on health benefits of safe vegetables",
    "Priority cards enabling LMI consumers to purchase safe vegetables at reasonable prices",
    "Training and communication on best practices across the supply chain",
    "Supporting producer-consumer linkages through retail and marketing integration",
    "Short supply chain via direct sale point at company campus",
    "Land consolidation policies to address fragmented production",
    "Short supply chain via local Women's Unions organizing residential vegetable supply"
  ),
  Selected = c("", "", "", "", "", "", "", "✓", "", "")
)

kable(interventions, 
      caption = "Table S1. Candidate interventions identified during the workshop, 
      evaluated against feasibility, actor availability, and expected effectiveness.") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE) %>%
  row_spec(8, bold = TRUE)
```

## Selected Intervention

Two short supply chain interventions received the highest votes. 
The Women's Union option was excluded on the third criterion — 
consultations confirmed that existing organizational responsibilities 
limit capacity for additional roles. The on-campus direct sale model 
was selected for modelling and piloting.
